Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & next steps

Hi Sofia + Tom,

Thanks for the time earlier today. Quick recap of what we heard and the suggested next steps so we're all aligned.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Current reranking pipeline is expensive and brittle: batch embeddings + external reranker causing high token costs and occasional latency spikes during peak hours.
- Need streaming outputs for live search UX (don't want the 2-3s wait per query).
- Desire structured outputs (JSON schema) from model responses to avoid downstream parsing fragility.
- Need function/tool-calling to invoke internal services (e.g., account lookups) without hitting rate limits.
- Compliance: data residency in US and audit logs retained for 12 months.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Prototype a hybrid approach: use Redwood embeddings for candidate generation + lightweight on-device (or managed) reranker to reduce token cost.
2) Validate streaming + structured outputs for the search UI with a 200-400ms initial token latency target.
3) Evaluate function calling for account lookups and event emission flows.
4) Establish a 4-week POC with sample traffic to measure cost/latency delta.

Integration / product fit notes:
- SDK: our Node + Python SDKs support streaming responses and function calling; we'll send a short code sample for your front-end flow.
- Structured outputs: we can enforce response schemas via our structured-output helpers and do lightweight schema validation server-side.
- Embeddings + reranking: recommend using our embeddings endpoint for vectors and Redwood reranker or an external on-prem component depending on latency constraints.
- Streaming: continuous streaming is supported; we'll show sample partial-output handling for your React front-end.

Next steps (owners & timing):
- Marissa: Share integration MPA + high-level SOW draft (attached), EOD Thu (Feb 19). [Attachment: redwood-integration-mpa.pdf, finexa-sow-draft.docx]
- Dev: Schedule a technical deep-dive to walk the SDK samples, function-calling patterns, and embedding pipeline, propose Fri (Feb 20) or Mon (Feb 23).
- Sofia/Tom: Confirm sample dataset & peak QPS for the POC, and any IP/data restrictions for the sandbox environment.
- Rachel: Provide cost estimate ranges for the POC and a Dedicated capacity vs hosted comparison.

Wanted to call out one potential fit detail: if you want to push reranking off the managed runtime (to save token costs) we can recommend a quantized ONNX reranker that sits in your VPC and calls Redwood for embeddings only, gives you predictable cost with sub-50ms local reranking.

Please reply with preferred time for the deep-dive and confirm the dataset we'll use. Happy to iterate the SOW based on your procurement needs.

Thanks,

Great to meet everyone on the call, thanks for the detailed questions. Per follow-up, I'm pasting the high-level SDK patterns and a short checklist of items we'll need from Finexa to get the POC running.

1) SDK patterns (Node / Python) — streaming + structured output + function calling
- Streaming: use the SDK stream handler to process partial tokens and render incremental results in the UI; it supports resumable streams and backpressure.
- Structured outputs: we recommend defining a JSON schema and using the SDK's schema_enforce flag to validate outputs server-side; invalid responses can route to a fallback model.
- Function calling: SDK supports typed function signatures; the runtime will populate arguments when confident and include provenance metadata in the response.

Sample pseudo-code (Node):
```js
const resp = await redwood.chat.stream({
  model: 'redwood-llama-3b-quant',
  messages: [{role: 'user', content: query}],
  functions: [/* bankLookup, logEvent */],
  schema: {type: 'object', properties: {accountId: {type: 'string'}}},
});
resp.on('partial', (chunk) => renderChunk(chunk));
resp.on('function_call', (call) => invokeInternal(call));
```

2) POC checklist (what we need from Finexa)
- Redacted 50k query sample (CSV or Parquet)
- Peak/sustained QPS and expected concurrency patterns (we have the 120 peak / 30-40 sustained noted)
- Any IP/data classification notes and required logging/audit windows
- Test credentials for the sandbox environment (we can provide ephemeral keys)

3) Proposed timeline
- Week 0: sandbox provisioning + SOW signing
- Weeks 1-3: integration + run sample traffic (measure latency, token cost)
- Week 4: results, recommendations, decision on Dedicated vs hosted for production

Attachments: integration playbook and a short SDK README (linked to the Drive folder in the invite). I'll also add the DocuSign SOW link once Marissa finalizes the MPA.

If helpful, I can also spin up a short demo repo with the React streaming handler by Mon EOD.
